title: The cmsis_compiler.h in CMSIS v5 is missing support for starm-clang
body: Hi, In my project I tried switching from GNU toolchain to starm-clang. I can build the project, and it runs fine on the target but there's a rather perplexing problem in the CMSIS header files. Link to a code branch which reproduces the problem is https://github.com/anttikes/usb-fm-radio/tree/swap-to-clangd Opening "Core/Src/i2s.c" one can see a warning stemming from the header file: The cause seems clear: the "cmsis_compiler.h" file is missing any #ifdef statements related to starm-clang. There is a row for "Arm Compiler 6" which apparently uses clang but this is probably a completely different toolset from starm-clang.

comments.author: MKISTM
comments.body:
Hello @anttikes,

Thank you for your report. Currently, we do not have plans to support the starm-clang compiler in the STM32CubeF0 firmware.
Thank you for your understanding, I will proceed with closing the issue.

BR,
Mohamed.

comments.author: ALABSTM

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @mmerlo,

The deployment of submodules is ongoing and the next step is to extend it to the middleware libraries. However, even though the USB Device library is replaced by a submodule, this does not mean it will automatically point on the latest version. A version upgrade of the library must happen only in the frame of a new release of the firmware.

Regarding a good way to navigate the repos, I suggest you look into the **README.md** file of the [STM32Cube_MCU_Overall_Offer](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32Cube_MCU_Overall_Offer) repo, where all repositories related to the STM32 **MCU** offer are listed.

Please note similar repositories are also available in the **pinned** section on top of the organization's main page, which are related to the STM32 **MPU** and **AI** offers.

One last hint to keep in mind and that could help understanding how repos are managed. Along with the STM32CubeF0 firmware, to take this one as an example, the different **components** it is made of (**i.e.**, CMSIS Device interfaces, HAL-LL drivers, BSP drivers, and MW libraries) are also published in **dedicated** repositories.  Only projects (**i.e.**, demos, applications and examples) are embedded within the firmware repository.

This proved to be very useful for users only interested in those components, not in the whole firmware. This also allows us to deploy the submodules.

I hope I could answer your questions. Please, do not hesitate otherwise.

With regards,

And `RCC_CR2_HSI48RDY_BitNumber` should be set to 17:

title: -Woverflow warning caused by HAL CRC function
body:
Hello, this warning started showing recently when I build my project:

`../Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F0xx/Include/stm32f0xx.h:198:41: warning: overflow in conversion from 'int' to 'uint8_t' {aka 'volatile unsigned char'} changes value from '(int)hcrc->Instance->IDR & -256' to '0' [-Woverflow]`

The offending line is here in the de-init function:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/blob/830a0e950d421c17abff57a2ea1e977870355519/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_crc.c#L205

I have two suggestions for fixes:

1. Use instead the macro from stm32f0xx.h   `CLEAR_REG(hcrc->Instance->IDR);`
2. Use instead the macro from the CRC header file  ` __HAL_CRC_SET_IDR(hcrc, 0);`

I'll leave it to you to select the best fix as I may not be aware of any knock-on effects.

I would very much appreciate if this change could be made, since I usually aim for 0 errors and 0 warnings for any released firmware and this warning is the only one I have currently. With it being in the driver code I cannot simply make the change myself.

title: Missing ";" in cmsis_os.h, FreeRTOS - CMSIS V1.11.x
body:
**Describe the set-up**
Programming a STM32F072B
With STM32CubeIDE
Version: 1.7.0
Build: 10852_20210715_0634 (UTC)
and
STM32CubeMX - STM32 Device Configuration Tool
Version: 6.3.0-RC5
Build: 20210714-1111 (UTC)


**Describe the bug**
I get this build error:
`C:/Users/User/STM32Cube/Repository/STM32Cube_FW_F0_V1.11.3/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/CMSIS_RTOS/cmsis_os.h:825:1: error: expected ';' before 'extern'
  825 | extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name`


**How To Reproduce**
1.1 Create a FreeRTOS project for a STM32F072B with the FreeRTOS API-CMSIS V1
1.2 Create an `osMailQDef(writeAnalog_mail, 2, analogData_t);` in the main.h
1.3 In `main.c`, put that code:
```
#define osObjectsExternal
#include "main.h"
main(){
     writeAnalog_mail = osMailCreate(osMailQ(writeAnalog_mail), NULL);
}
```

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).
In the file name is : "cmsis_os.h".
````
//  ==== Mail Queue Management Functions ====

#if (defined (osFeature_MailQ)  &&  (osFeature_MailQ != 0))     // Mail Queues available

/// \brief Create a Mail Queue Definition.
/// \param         name          name of the queue
/// \param         queue_sz      maximum number of messages in queue
/// \param         type          data type of a single message element
/// \note CAN BE CHANGED: The parameter to \b osMailQDef shall be consistent but the
///       macro body is implementation specific in every CMSIS-RTOS.
#if defined (osObjectsExternal)  // object is external
#define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \
extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name \
extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name
#else                            // define the object
#define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \
struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name \
const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name =  \
{ (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name) }
#endif 
````

3. The use case that generates the problem.
Write what is explained in "1" and simply build. An error should appear. The way to solve it, which worked for me was to add ';' at the end of `extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name`, `extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name`, `struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name`, `const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name = { (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name)} `,
The end result should look like this:
````
#if defined (osObjectsExternal)  // object is external
#define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \
extern struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name; \
extern osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name;
#else                            // define the object
#define osMailQDef(name, queue_sz, type) \
struct os_mailQ_cb *os_mailQ_cb_##name; \
const osMailQDef_t os_mailQ_def_##name =  \
{ (queue_sz), sizeof (type), (&os_mailQ_cb_##name) } ;
#endif 
````


**Additional context**
Maybe look and test all "extern" definition if there is any ";" missing.

title: Including `stm32f0xx_ll_adc.h` introduces ` `-Wunused-parameter` warnings into client code
body:
The offending section is below:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/blob/4390ff6bfb693104cf97192f98c3dc9e3a7c296a/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f0xx_ll_adc.h#L1411-L1415

The parameter `Register` is not used.  However, because this is a function body defined in a header file, any _users_ of this library wind up hitting compiler warnings for this oversight.  I build my projects with `-Werror`, and so this becomes an error for me.  I don't know for sure what the project's preferred fix is but a couple that come to mind (some could work in combination):

* Don't define the body of this function in the header file
* Eliminate this unnecessary `Register` argument from the function definition
* Add a `(void) Register;` line to the function to appease the compiler and eliminate the warning

Thanks for your consideration

- Are you using our MCU as master with another MCU (2 MCUs used) ?  Or are you using only one MCU and declaring different I2C instances as masters within your application ?

comments.author: eelmor
comments.body:
Hello @ASELSTM,

1. I'm not sure about the exact matching criteria as I don't know the exact data being sent by the other master, but the I2C_ISR ADDR bit keeps getting set when using the I2C peripheral in Master mode which stalls the peripheral. I don't see any reason to set the OA1EN bit when used as Master only.
2. Yes, two masters on the I2C bus (2x MCU).

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @eelmor,



Referring to your feedback, the behavior you are detecting means that you didn't set an own address value on the initialization phase. Indeed, an own address should be set since that in the initialization phase the I2C don't know if it is configured as master or slave.

Even if you use the device as a master,  you need to set an own address since that the I2C is set as slave by default.  The I2C becomes master once the start bit is generated and becomes slave back after a sop generation as mentioned  in the [reference manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/dm00031936-stm32f0x1stm32f0x2stm32f0x8-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) within section **"26.4.4 Mode selection"**.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47858836/121534647-52e96800-c9f9-11eb-8339-3c5c8d4c5ed5.png)


With regards,

comments.author: eelmor
comments.body:
Hello @ASELSTM ,

If I'm not setting a slave address, HAL should not set the OA1EN bit.

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @eelmor,

As mentioned above, the STM32 I2C instances are by default configured as slave unless they are used as master by calling the master mode APIs.  So that, at initialization phase, since the I2C is set as slave mode during this phase, an address is necessary to allow the I2C to recognize it self. 

To resume, the I2C instances are operating in slave mode unless a start condition is generated so that setting a slave address is primordial and mandatory.  Even if you are not setting any address in your source code, the general call address **0x00** is taken by default and OA1EN will be set anyway.

In order to allow a correct use of the I2C, a correct address (different from general call address `0x00`) should be set as slave address.

Hope this would help you.

With regards,

comments.author: eelmor
comments.body:
Hello @ASELSTM,

It doesn't help me. How can I initialize I2C in HAL without slave mode active? Right now I need workarounds to do this. I don't want it to respond to any address.

BR,
Jon

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @eelmor,

It is actually not possible as the I2C is designed to operate in salve mode unless it generates a START condition. From an IP design point of view, the I2C is always configured as slave by default.

In multi-master mode there must be a sequence between the applications to manage the call to the HAL API in synchronization. Thus, Master 1 call Master_Transmit, until end then Master 2 call  Master_Transmit until end. Please make sure that you are using the right sequence within your application.

Please allow me then to close this thread. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

comments.author: eelmor
comments.body: All that's needed is for OA1EN to stay cleared during HAL Init when I don't specify a slave address and it works correctly. I want to be able to do this without hacking HAL. How can you say that it's not possible?

title: UART ISR becomes interrupt bound due to incomplete implemenation of UART Recieve Timeout
body:
**Describe the set-up**
* Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RC
* IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1
* HAL: 1.11.0

**Describe the bug**
When the UART receive timeout is enabled, it is possible the ISR executes without clearing the interrupt.  Consequently, the ISR is continuously called using 100% of the microprocessor time.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project.
A serial connection which uses intercharacter timeout to indicate the end of message.

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).
HAL_UART_IRQHandler() ISR function in stm32f0xx_hal_uart.c

3. The use case that generates the problem.
A serial connection that uses intercharacter timeout to detect 'end of message'.  The receive timeout is enabled using the following functions:

```
HAL_UART_ReceiverTimeout_Config(mHuart, mBitsPerCharacter);
HAL_UART_EnableReceiverTimeout(mHuart);

SET_BIT(mHuart->Instance->CR1, USART_CR1_RTOIE);  // See Note

```
Note: The receive timeout interrupt has to be enabled manually

4. How we can reproduce the problem.
You need to generate a receive timeout interrupt and ensure no other UART interrupts are pending.  Following this condition the ISR will become interrupt bound.

**Additional context**

The defect is in the ISR function HAL_UART_IRQHandler().  The following code:

```
if ((errorflags != 0U)
      && (((cr3its & USART_CR3_EIE) != 0U)
          || ((cr1its & (USART_CR1_RXNEIE | USART_CR1_PEIE)) != 0U)))

```
should be:

```
if ((errorflags != 0U)
      && (((cr3its & USART_CR3_EIE) != 0U)
          || ((cr1its & (USART_CR1_RXNEIE | USART_CR1_PEIE | USART_CR1_RTOIE)) != 0U)))

```
Notice **USART_CR1_RTOIE** is not present in the original code.

When this is fixed, can you also integrate the enabling and disabling of the receive timeout interrupt into the HAL so it doesn't have to be done manually. 

**Screenshots**
None

title: Conflicting types for 'assert_failed'
body:
**Describe the set-up**
Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32F030RCTx.
IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1

**Describe the bug**
When **USE_FULL_ASSERT** is enabled, STM32CubeMX generates this function in _main.c_:

`void assert_failed(char *file, uint32_t line)`

however the prototype in _stm32f0xx_hal_conf.h_ has been changed to this:

`void assert_failed(uint8_t* file, uint32_t line);`

This causes a compile error from GCC **"error: conflicting types for 'assert_failed'"**

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project
The application uses STM32CubeMX built in assert mechanism.  This defect occurs at compile time.

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...)
 _stm32f0xx_hal_conf.h_ (which is generated from the _stm32f0xx_hal_conf_template.h_) has been updated with a new prototype, but the function body in _main.c_ has not been updated.

3. The use case that generates the problem
Compiling the application.

4. How we can reproduce the problem

- Create a project in STM32CubeMX using this mcu package.  Ensure Enable Full Assert is ticked (Project Manager\Code Generator\Hal Settings).
- Generate the code and compile the project.  A compile error is generated as in the description above.

**Additional context**
It looks like someone updated the prototype but forgot to update the body. The funny thing is _**uint8_t***_ is not correct anyway. I think it should be changed to _**const char***_, or at least keep it at _**char***_

**Screenshots**
None
